items.summary: Confirmed and upheld against source. 06.01.02's refund surface is specified for exactly five triggers — teacher departure voluntary and involuntary (:150-159), academy closure (edge case 11), GDPR erasure (edge case 31), an upheld chargeback (edge case 13) and a failed refund (edge case 32) — and none of them is a student changing their mind. Yet edge case 12 (:200) tells the student in product copy 'Credits are with {teacher}. To stop lessons with them, request a refund — with the refund path stated, not hidden', and the credit lifecycle at :78 carries 'granted ──refund──> refunded (to the PURCHASER — D-08)' with no trigger condition on the arrow. The calendar half is equally unspecified: 06.01.01's States table (:153-168) has no student-ended state, Completed is confined to fixed-count series (:149), and 06.01.03 covers only the teacher side ('Teacher cancels the entire series (quits)' :143, which explicitly routes the pack question away to 06.01.02). Classified OWNER, not mechanical: no location drifted from a canonical value — the value was never set, and every available answer changes what the product does for a paying user and carries consumer-protection exposure (06.01.02 DT-02). Nothing was fixed. Two tracked question rows were added so the gap cannot be silently invented downstream: canonical 06.01.02 Q-09 (money) and 06.01.01 Q-05 (tenancy), each naming the other, both User / `/create-prd`.
items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED — Can a student stop lessons mid-pack and get their money back, and what happens to their standing slot when they do?

WHY THIS IS ON YOUR DESK
The spec tree currently tells a student to do something it never specified. 06.01.02 edge case 12 refuses to move credits between teachers (correct — D-01 scopes credits to a teacher because the price is teacher-specific) and then sends the student to a refund path with the words 'To stop lessons with them, request a refund'. That path does not exist. Refunds are defined only for teacher departure, academy closure, GDPR erasure, chargeback, and failed-refund handling. The credit lifecycle diagram draws a `granted → refunded` arrow with no trigger written on it. Meanwhile 06.01.01's series state machine offers no way for a student to end an ongoing series at all: it can only lapse from non-payment, complete (fixed-count only), or be ended by the teacher. A student who wants to stop today has exactly one specified route — stop paying and wait out the 2-occurrence / 14-day At-Risk grace — which releases the teacher's slot late, tells the teacher nothing until the balance bites, and is indistinguishable from someone who just forgot to top up.

WHAT IS ALREADY DECIDED AND CONSTRAINS YOU
- D-06: teacher earnings accrue on delivery or a policy burn, never on purchase. So the money for unspent lessons is still on the platform. A refund is mechanically possible without clawing anything back from a teacher — that is why teacher departure and academy closure can be made whole. Nothing blocks a voluntary refund technically.
- D-04: expiry no longer destroys value; an unspent credit degrades to a residual (cash paid, purchase currency, pinned FX, still teacher-scoped) redeemable against that teacher's current list price. This gives you a middle option that is not cash.
- D-08: any refund routes to the PURCHASER, not the student. In a minors-heavy domain that is usually the parent, and edge case 26 (two separated guardians, one child) means it must route to the right purchaser's pack.
- D-12: credit transfer between teachers is a departure REMEDY, never a feature, because at-will transfer is 'shopping with a specific teacher's money'. Note the trap: refund-at-will followed by re-purchase with teacher B lands in exactly the same place by a longer route. If you grant an unconditional voluntary refund you have overturned D-12 by accident.
- 06.01.01 D-03: tenure binds to paid-through status, and its reasoning is that 'a student who paid for an hour owns that hour'. That argues against releasing a slot the moment a student asks to stop.
- D-14: the pack builder shows the teacher their forward liability — hours committed at an effective discounted rate. A discount priced against volume that can be unwound at will is not the commitment the teacher was shown.

FOUR SUB-DECISIONS, EACH GENUINELY OPEN
(a) Is a voluntary refund of UNSPENT credits granted on request, granted at the teacher's discretion, or refused outright?
(b) If granted, is it cash to the purchaser at the price paid, or conversion to D-04 residual with no cash out? Residual is the cheaper answer and is already built — it keeps the money with that teacher, which preserves D-12, but it does not help the parent whose child has quit the instrument.
(c) Does anything attach — a notice period, a clawback of the pack discount (a 16%-off 10-pack refunded at the discounted £38 after six lessons hands back money the discount was priced against volume for), teacher consent?
(d) Does the standing slot release immediately, or at the paid-through date? Immediate release contradicts D-03's own reasoning; paid-through release means a teacher cannot resell a Tuesday for weeks after being told the student is gone.

WHAT THIS IS NOT
Not 06.01.02 Q-01. That question is narrowed by D-04 to a single axis — whether RESIDUAL, which only arises at expiry, is withdrawable as cash. This is live credits held by a student who wants to stop now, which Q-01 never reaches.
Not 06.02.04's 'Student converts, then quits after two lessons | Normal churn; nothing special'. That row acknowledges the scenario and specifies nothing.

THREE SHAPES, FOR ORIENTATION ONLY — the choice is yours
1. NO VOLUNTARY REFUND. Credits are an entitlement; you bought lessons with this teacher, D-04 means nothing expires, use them whenever. Cheapest, most defensible for the teacher, cleanest against D-12 — and the answer most exposed to consumer-protection challenge in the EU/UK, in a market whose buyer is a parent. Requires deleting the refund promise from edge case 12's copy.
2. RESIDUAL ON REQUEST, NO CASH. A student may convert unspent credits to residual at any time and stop; the money stays teacher-scoped and redeemable, the pack discount is unwound to list price on conversion. Preserves D-12 exactly, uses machinery D-04 already built, gives the honest 'we stopped' path a real answer — but a parent whose child has quit for good still has money they can only spend on lessons they will not take.
3. CASH REFUND OF UNEARNED VALUE, WITH FRICTION. Refund at the effective paid price minus a stated unwind of the pack discount, to the purchaser, with the slot released at the paid-through date rather than immediately. Best for the parent and safest under consumer law; needs an explicit carve-out saying it does not reopen D-12, and needs the teacher's forward-liability view (D-14) to show refundable exposure so a teacher is not surprised.

WHOEVER ANSWERS: answer both ids together. 06.01.02 Q-09 is the money; 06.01.01 Q-05 is the slot. Answered apart, they produce a balance and a calendar that disagree.
